full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 78 of 2006 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Satkhira Sadar for declaration of title and further declaration that the S.A. record is wrong with an additional prayer of partition contending inter alia, that the suit properties appertaining to C.S. khatian No.771 of Mouza Madhabkhali under P.S. Satkhira originally belonged, to one Enamul Hoque Biswas comprising an area of 54 decimals of land under whom one Bagan Behara Sarder was a korfa tenant and the under khatian was 773. Due to arrear of rent for non-payment of the same by the korfa tenant Bagan Behara the landlord preferred a rent suit and obtained a decree therein. Thereafter, in decree Execution Case No.221 of 1952 the property was auction-purchased by the landlord and subsequently decided to settle with the land. The plaintiff's father namely Madar Sarder at a salami of Taka 50/- and yearly rental of Taka 5/- took settlement of the property. In favour of the landlord Enamul Hoque Biswas Madar Sarder executed a registered kabuliyat in respect of the land on 25.02.1956. Thereafter; Madar Sarder out of the total 54 decimals of land sold out 10½ decimals of land in favour of the defendant No.5 and delivered possession. Subsequently; by another transfer deed dated 31.10.1966 Madar Sarder transferred 8 decimals of land in favour of one Abdul Khaleque who by a subsequent transfer deed dated 17.12.1990 transferred that 8 decimals of land along with other lands in all 27 decimals in favour of the plaintiffs No. 1 and 2. Madar Sarder died leaving behind four sons Abdus Salam Sarder and others, one daughter Anwara Khatun and wife Meherful bibi. In this way the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land by way of inheritance and their purchase deeds. During S.A. operation due to ailing condition of Madar Sarder his brother Nur Mohammad was entrusted responsibility to record the name of Mather Sarder, but Nur Mohammad Sarder the brother of Madar Sarder recorded his name along with, his relations instead of his brother. The defendants threatened the plaintiffs by virtue of that record and denied to effect partition which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant No.5 who is the opposite party No.1 of the revisional application in short is thus that Bagan Behara Sarder was the korfa tenant under the original owner of the suit property Enamul Hoque Biswas. Due to arrears of rent a Rent Suit was filed by the landlord against Bagan Behara and the landlord obtained decree and in Decree Execution Case No.221 of 1952 the property was auction-purchased by the landlord. Thereafter, while the landlord proposed to settle the land, two brothers Madar Sarder and Nur Mohammad Sardar, son of Bagan Behara Sardar decided to take settlement and accordingly settlement was taken from the joint fund of the family and for joint interest of the family members but the kabuliyat dated 25.02.1956 was executed by the elder brother of the family Madar Sarder. The property was possessed in ejmali by two brothers and their mother and accordingly the S.A. record 602 was prepared in their names. At the demise of the brothers the property was devolved upon the heirs of two brothers. In this way the heirs of Madar Studer by way of inheritance acquired 27 decimals of land. During life time by two sets of kabla deeds Madar Sarder transferred 10½ decimals of land in favour the defendant No.5. The remaining brother Nur Mohammad by a registered kabla dated 09.08.1984 transferred his land in favour of the defendant no.5. The story of acquisition of the land by only one brother namely Madar Sarder is false and to deprive the other brother and his mother this was stated within the pleadings of the plaintiffs out of ill motive. The defendant not being the exclusive owner of 48 decimals of land have been owning and possessing that portion of land and the D.P. khatian accordingly prepared in his name. He has mutated his name and paying rent regularly. The plaintiffs on false allegation filed the suit which is liable to be dismissed. 

 7. The learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not taking the view that the settlement of the suit land in favour of Madar Sarder is genuine and that was for his own interest and money. The learned Advocate further submits that the kabuliyat which was a registered instrument in favour of the landlord was exclusively executed and registered by Madar Sarder and the learned District Judge have failed to appreciate the facts of the case including documentary evidence which is on records. There is nothing on record to hold such a view that the money for taking settlement was obtained from the joint fund of the joint family as alleged from the side of the contesting defendant. As a member of Muslim community there is no provision in the Mohammadan Law that joint family concept can be considered legal and as such the learned District Judge in taking decision over the pertinent point of the suit holding the view that as a member of a joint family for the interest of others Madar Sarder acquired the property is an error apparent on the face of the record. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned lower appellate court in his findings and observation once held that Madar Sarder as a member of joint family on behalf of his brother and mother and for himself obtained the settlement from the landlord and executed the kabuliyat but he has given a contradictory decision that the kabuliyat dated 25.02.1956 is an ineffective document and by this document nothing was accrued in favour of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate submits that, Exhibit-3 is the kabla deed dated 31.10.1966 by which the two brothers namely Madar Sarder and Nur Mohammad Sarder sold land in favour of one Abdul Khaleque. From this kabla deed it appears that Nur Mohammad sold his land not from, the suit khatian but from different khatian and on the other hand Madar Sarder transferred his land from the suit khatian which proves that the settlement was taken by Madar Sarder himself for his own interest in respect of the disputed property. Besides this; the defendant no.1 who is the son of Nur Mohammad after giving evidence proved the case of the plaintiffs in taking settlement by Madar Sarder alone not with his brother Nur Mohammad which is not properly addressed by the learned appellate court below. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the plaintiffs paid rent in respect of the suit property till 1997 and taking advantage of wrong S.A. record the defendants mutated their names illegality and despite the S.A. record is not the document of title, the same is not properly appreciated by the learned appellate court and in this way the appellate court misdirected himself to the contents of Exhibit-3 the kabla deed dated 31.10.1966 and failed to assess other evidence on records in its true perspective. There is non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable. 

 10. On perusal of the case records it transpires that admittedly the property originally belonged to the landlord Enamul Hoque Biswas and Bagan Behara Sardar was a korfa tenant under the Ex-landlord. It is also an admitted position that there was an under khatian of the concerned C.S. khatian No.771 of suit mouza Madhabkhali and the area of the land was 54 decimals. It is also admitted that for arrears of rent the property was pot to an auction and the landlord Enamul Hoque Biswas auction-purchased the same. In a Rent Execution Case No.221 of 1952 the property which was auction-purchased by the landlord was proposed for settlement. It is the case of the plaintiffs that their predecessor Madar Sarder for his own interest and by his own money took settlement from the Ex-landlord and executed a registered kabuliyat on 25.02.1956. Vis-a-vis; it has been contended from the side of the contesting defendant-opposite party that after the death of Bagan Behara Sarder his two sons Madar Sarder and Nur Mohammad Sarder along with their mother were in a joint family and joint mess and it was decided by the two brothers that they would take settlement and accordingly on behalf of all the elder brother Madar Sarder executed the "kabuliyat" in favour of the landlord. Subsequently, during the S.A. record the elder brother recorded his name with his brother and mother's name in khatian No.602 which was finally published. In the instant case, the pertinent question which is the matter of adjudication is such as to whether the property is acquired alone by Madar Sarder or on behalf of all of the family members left behind Bagan Behara Sarder. It is a fact that the learned trial court during passing his judgment and decree examined six oral witnesses from the sides of the respective parties and decided the pertinent point in favour of the plaintiffs. Subsequently, the lower appellate court decided that the settlement in the name of Madar Sarder never effected and by virtue of that settlement nothing was acquired. Neither Madar Sarder nor Nur Mohammad Sarder nor their mother acquired any portion of land of the suit holding by virtue of the kabuliyat deed dated 25.02.1956 which has been marked as Exhibit-5 and Exhibit-`Ga' respectively from the sides of the respective parties. The proposition of law as cited with the recital of the impugned judgment and decree under the ambit of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act appears to be sound and cogent. Apart from this; the settlement followed by the kabuliyat marked as exhibit-5 was not completed as there is nothing to hold such a view that the Zaminder or the landlord ever obtained any salami or accepted rent from the settlement holder. Besides this; Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1954 which takes it effect from 16.05.1951 have imposed a legal embargo in giving settlement by the landlord in favour of anybody. It has been properly appreciated by the learned District Judge, Satkhira in his findings. 

 11. Scrutinizing the corresponding C.S. Khatian No. 773 and its subsequent S.A. Khatian No. 602 it transpires that the land measuring an area of 54 decimals have been recorded in the name of two brothers and mother. It is on records that during the life time of Madar Sarder the S.A. record was not challenged by him and after his demise it has been challenged from the side of his successors the plaintiffs. It is a fact that during life time Madar Sarder by a registered kabla deed dated 31.10.1966 (Ext.-3) transferred some land in favour of one Abdul Khaleque and subsequently 19 decimals of land was transferred in favour of the plaitniff No.4 by a separate kabla deed dated 17.12.1990 and plaintiff No. 1 and 2 by virtue of their kabla deed acquired 19 decimals of land which has been properly addressed by the leaned lower appellate court. It is also not denied from any corner that in the year 1969 the predecessor of the plaintiffs Madar Sarder executed and registered two kabala deeds dated 10.06.1969 and 02.12.1969 which has been marked as Exhibits-"Gha" and "Uma". It is apparent from the face of the document that the kabla deed dated 31.10.1966 which has been marked as Exhibit-3 two brothers Madar Sarder and Nur Mohammad Sarder sold out some land in favour of Abdul Khaleque. From the contents of this document it appears that Nur Mohammad transferred different land with that of the suit khatian in favour of the purchaser and from the suit khatian Madar Sarder sold out some portion of land in favour of the purchaser. Apart from this; if we evaluate the oral evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties we find that the plaintiffs in support of their respective case have examined three witnesses and the defendants in support of their case have adduced three witnesses. The plaintiff No.1 is the P.W.1 Abdus Salam Sarder. From his admission it has come to the notice of the court that his father Mader Sarder was aware about the S.A. record during his life time and he disclosed about the S.A. khatian before this plaintiff No.1. Hence; the learned appellate court rightly held that Madar Sarder during his life time did not raise any objection against the record of rights. Secondly; the plaintiffs relied upon the evidence of P.W.2 Abul Kalam who is the defendant No.1 to this suit. Admittedly, he is the son of Nur Mohammad and a man of 50 years at the time of giving deposition. In his averment he has stated that the plaintiffs do possess the suit land from 1990 and before them their predecessors possessed. Within his testimony it is apparent from his admission that he had no knowledge about the land prior to 1990. In the last portion of his deposition he has frankly conceded that he has no knowledge about the suit properties. The possession witness of the plaintiffs P.W.3 Khalilur Rahman tried to state in his examination-in-chief that he knows the suit land from the year 1990 and this land is being possessed by the plaintiff Salem, but scanning his cross-examination it transpires that he practically does not know the suit land. He admits that he has no land beside the suit land and he cannot say the boundaries of the suit land and also cannot say the quantum of the suit land. Under the ambit of sections 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act it is the incumbent duty of the plaintiffs that they are to establish their case by credible evidence, but in the instant case; it can be easily held that the witnesses those who are coming from the side of the plaintiffs are not competent and trustworthy and they have totally failed to discharge their onus in proving the case of the plaintiffs. Vis-à-vis; the oral evidence led from the side of the defendants go to show that the witness No.1 is the defendant No.5 himself who in support of his pleadings deposed. The other two witnesses Abul Hashem and Gobinda Chandra tried to corroborate the defendant No.5. The learned appellate court in his observation and findings assessed the evidence on records and rebutted the findings of the trial court adverting evidence.
